description: ALOHA is the hazard modelling program of the CAMEO software suite, which the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration provide to plan for and respond to chemical emergencies. A user enters details of a real or potential chemical release and ALOHA estimates threat zones for toxic gas clouds, flammable gas clouds, boiling liquid expanding vapour explosions (BLEVEs), jet fires, pool fires and vapour cloud explosions. Threat zones are shown on a grid, with red for the worst hazard level and orange and yellow for decreasing levels, and can be plotted in MARPLOT, Esri ArcMap, Google Earth and Google Maps. Version 5.4.7 (September 2016) is a free download for Windows and Mac, with a chemical library that includes Design Institute for Physical Properties data and toxic levels of concern, a fact sheet, worked examples and technical documentation of the models and equations. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): EPA web policy: EPA-produced content is in the public domain unless otherwise specified (software licence not stated separately). Caveats: the program has not been updated since 2016 and is supported only on older operating system versions. For simulation it gives quick consequence estimates of chemical releases for emergency planning, natech scenarios and exposure of nearby infrastructure. Related catalogue records include RAPID-N and the EPA Risk Management Plan information.
